{{short description|Hungarian mathematician}}
'''Zsolt Baranyai''' (June 23, 1948 in [[Budapest]] &ndash; April 6, 1978) was a Hungarian [[mathematician]] known for his work in [[combinatorics]]. 

He graduated from [[Fazekas Mihály Gimnázium (Budapest)|Fazekas High School]] where he was a classmate of [[László Lovász]], [[Miklós Laczkovich]], and [[Lajos Pósa (mathematician)|Lajos Pósa]]. He studied mathematics at [[Eötvös Loránd University]] and went on to become a lecturer in the Analysis Department. He earned his Ph.D. in 1975 and was posthumously awarded the [[Candidate of Sciences|Candidate degree]] of the [[Hungarian Academy of Sciences]] in 1978. 

Baranyai is best known for his [[Baranyai's theorem|theorem]] on the decompositions of complete [[hypergraph|hypergraphs]], which solved a long-standing open problem.<ref>{{harvtxt|van Lint|Wilson|2001}}. Chapter 38, "Baranyai's theorem", pp. 536–541.</ref> In addition to his mathematical pursuits, Baranyai was also a professional musician who played the [[Recorder (musical instrument)|recorder]]. He died while touring Hungary with the Bakfark Consort in a car accident after a concert.<ref>{{citation|title=A Course in Combinatorics|first1=J. H.|last1=van Lint|first2=R. M.|last2=Wilson|publisher=Cambridge University Press|year=2001|isbn=9780521006019|page=540|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=5l5ps2JkyT0C&pg=PA540}}.</ref>
